title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: many adults lack immediate aid to believe — Bellarmine's 'posse' via creatures is a miserable defense of esse
pass_a_gloss: Finally among adults themselves very many there are, Bellarmine confessing, ibid. c. 8. unto whom sufficient help unto believing is not immediately granted, but is understood as granted only in this sense, that they can know through the creatures that God is, and can be stirred by God unto believing that God is, and that he is a rewarder unto them that seek him; and can by such faith be stirred unto praying unto God, and in this way (although destitute of the preaching of the Gospel) can obtain that they be illuminated in the knowledge of the faith either by God himself, or by an Angel, or by some man. How miserable this defense is, which when the question is instituted concerning being, answers only concerning being-able, I doubt not that you all understand. I wished only in passing to touch it, that you may see how ill founded is this proposition concerning sufficient grace given unto all and singular, which our disputers lay under as the most solid foundation of their cause. I add no more, because even if it be granted, it still does not make unto solid proof of the cause, as we showed from the beginning.
pass_b_english: Finally, among adults themselves, Bellarmine admits (ibid. c. 8), very many are not given immediate sufficient help to believe — only in this thin sense: they can know God through the creatures, can be stirred to believe that God is and rewards seekers, can be stirred by that faith to pray, and so (even without Gospel preaching) can obtain illumination in the faith from God, an angel, or some man. Miserable defense: the question is about what is, and the answer is only about what can be — you all see that. I touch it only in passing, to show how poorly founded is the claim that sufficient grace is given to every person, which our disputers lay as their cause's firmest base. I add nothing more: even if granted, it still does not solidly prove their cause, as we showed from the start.
source_text: Denique inter ipsos adultos quamplurimi sunt, fatente Bellarmino, ibid. c. 8. quibus sufficiens auxilium ad credendum non immediate conceditur, sed hoc solummodo sensu concessum intelligitur, quia possunt cognoscere per creaturas Deum esse, et possunt a Deo excitari ad credendum quod Deus sit, et quod inquirentibus se remunerator sit; et possunt tali fide excitari ad orandum Deum, et hoc modo (quamvis destituantur praedicatione Evangelii) possunt impetrare ut vel ab ipso Deo, vel ab Angelo, vel ab aliquo homine in cognitione fidei illuminentur. Quam misera sit haec defensio, quae cum quaestio instituatur de esse, respondet solummodo de posse, non dubito quin omnes intelligatis. Eam solummodo obiter perstringere volui, ut videatis quam male fundata sit haec propositio de sufficiente gratia omnibus et singulis donata, quam disputatores nostri substernunt tanquam solidissimum fundamentum causae suae. Plura non addo, quia licet concedatur, non tamen facit ad solidam causae probationem, uti ab initio ostendimus.
